story_type: solo sailor's boat failing in rough seas far offshore, swimmer climbs aboard, basket hoist
hook: Sailing alone, 60 miles out, and his boat was failing him.
narration: He was sailing alone, sixty miles off Cape Lookout, North Carolina, when his boat started failing him.
The forty foot sailboat Sassafras had lost its sea anchor, and its engines were giving him trouble.
At about four thirty in the morning, he called the Coast Guard.
A C-130 overhead tried to pass him a radio. It failed.
So a helicopter crew lowered a rescue swimmer into the water near the sailboat.
Swimmers often go in the water first, because a sailboat's swinging mast can foul a hoist cable over the deck.
[short pause] The swimmer climbed aboard, and the man made the decision to leave his boat.
At about eleven thirty, the crew hoisted them up to the helicopter.
outcome: The sailor was flown to Marine Corps Air Station Cherry Point in good condition.

A Coast Guard aircrew from Air Station Elizabeth City hoists a man sailing alone aboard the 40-foot sailboat Sassafras after it became disabled about 60 miles off Cape Lookout, North Carolina, on Dec. 15, 2015.
